stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 2 x^{3} + 9 x^{2} + 12 x + 4 \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether f has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = -2 \) and at \( x = 4 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = -2 \), f has a relative maximum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 4 \), f has no relative extremum because \( f'(4) = 180 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( f'(x) = 6 x^{2} + 18 x + 12 \), which factors as \( f'(x) = 6 \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 2\right) \).
\( f'(-2) = 0 \), so \( x = -2 \) is a critical point, while \( f'(4) = 180 \ne 0 \), so \( x = 4 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test f has a relative maximum at \( x = -2 \). At \( x = 4 \) the first derivative is not zero, so f has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.

options.label: At \( x = -2 \), f has a relative maximum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 4 \), f has no relative extremum because \( f'(4) = 180 \ne 0 \).
At \( x = -2 \), f has a relative minimum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 4 \), f has no relative extremum because \( f'(4) = 180 \ne 0 \).
options.derivation: the sign convention of the test reversed, so a negative second derivative is read as a minimum and a positive one as a maximum

options.label: At \( x = -2 \), f has an absolute maximum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 4 \), f has no relative extremum because \( f'(4) = 180 \ne 0 \).
options.derivation: the relative extremum from the second derivative test extended to an absolute one with no argument that it is the only critical point, which it is not

options.label: At \( x = -2 \), f has a relative maximum because \( f'(-2) = 0 \) and \( f''(-2) = -6 < 0 \); at \( x = 4 \), f has a relative minimum because \( f''(4) = 66 > 0 \).
options.derivation: the second derivative test also applied at x = 4, where the first derivative is not zero, and the sign of the second derivative there read as a classification
